newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine Menem says World Bank sees 4 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Menem says World Bank sees 4 pct growth.

text.p: A World Bank report says Argentina's economy will grow by about four percent in 1996, President Carlos Menem said Tuesday.

"I received a report from the World Bank a few hours ago, fresh out of the oven to use a baker's term, that talks of growth in Argentina this year of close to four percent, and for next year of around five percent in gross domestic product," Menem said.

"The report also tells us that poverty has fallen significantly in our country," he told reporters at the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange, where he was accompanying visiting Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo.

Argentina's economy contracted by 4.6 percent in 1995, after a sudden capital outflow triggered by Mexico's peso devaluation in late 1994. The economy shrank by 0.1 percent in the first half of this year.
